yaml.title: Better Code, Less Pain
yaml.subtitle: Developer tooling I use — and why you should care
yaml.author: Dr. Rowan Lindsay-Smith

markdown.markdown: ```text rt-demo/ ├── analysis.py └── data/ └── results.csv ``` ```bash python analysis.py ``` ::: {.fragment .big-question} I've sent you this repository. **Can you reproduce the figure?** ::: ::: {.notes} Demo: `demo-start` (00-start), then run `python analysis.py`. Ask: Which Python? Which pandas? Which matplotlib? How do you install them? Message: working on my computer is not the same as reproducible. ::: --- ## Before tooling: version control ```text working code → Git history → changes you can inspect or reverse ``` ::: {.fragment .takeaway} Version control is a record of deliberate changes—not a folder of `final_v3.py` files. ::: ::: {.notes} Git foundations: commit, diff, branch, recover. Anecdote: finding when an analysis changed. ::: --- ## Git is not GitHub ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="48%"} ### Git - local version-control system - commits, history and branches - works without GitHub ::: ::: {.column width="52%"} ### GitHub - hosts Git repositories - pull requests and collaboration - Actions and Dependabot ::: ::: ::: {.fragment .takeaway} **Git tracks changes. GitHub hosts and helps collaborate on them.** ::: ::: {.notes} Explain the difference. GitHub will reappear when demonstrating CI and Dependabot. ::: --- ## Reproducibility starts with the environment ```text Project │ ┌────────┴────────┐ │ │ pyproject.toml uv.lock │ │ what it needs exact resolution ``` ```bash uv sync uv run python analysis.py ``` ::: {.fragment .takeaway} Move knowledge **from the state of my laptop into the repository**. ::: ::: {.notes} `demo-next` -> 01-uv. Run `uv sync`, then `uv run python analysis.py`. Anecdote slot: dependency/environment problem from a real project. ::: --- ## Humans are bad linters ```python import pandas as pd import matplotlib.pyplot as plt # ... data = data[data["correct"] == True] ``` ::: {.fragment} ```bash uv run ruff check . uv run ruff check . --fix uv run ruff format . git diff ``` ::: ::: {.fragment .takeaway} If a computer can identify and fix something reliably, don't spend human attention on it. ::: ::: {.notes} `demo-next` -> 02-ruff. Run Ruff and let it fail. Then --fix, format, and show git diff. Distinguish formatter (appearance) from linter (suspicious/problematic constructs). ::: --- ## Make assumptions explicit ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"} ```python def analyse(file): ... ``` ::: ::: {.column width="55%"} ```python def analyse( file: Path, ) -> list[tuple[str, float]]: ... ``` ::: ::: ::: {.fragment} Which interface would you rather discover in somebody else's code? ::: ::: {.notes} `demo-next` -> 03-types. Temporarily pass a string instead of Path: `data_file = "data/results.csv"; results = analyse(data_file)`. Run `uv run pyright`; fix with Path and rerun. Keep pandas typing complications out of the live explanation. ::: --- ## Pyright: catch disagreement before execution ```python data_file = "data/results.csv" results = analyse(data_file) ``` ```text ┌──────── expected Path "data/results.csv" ────────✗ ``` ::: {.fragment} ```python data_file = Path("data/results.csv") results = analyse(data_file) ``` ::: ::: {.fragment .takeaway} Types make interfaces useful to **people and tools**. ::: --- ## “Just one more option…” ```text Analyse RTs │ ├── exclude errors? ├── trim? ├── mean or median? ├── exclude another case? └── just one more option... ``` ::: {.fragment} ```bash uv run pyright # ✓ uv run ruff check . # ✗ C901 ``` ::: ::: {.takeaway .fragment} Nobody deliberately writes the horrible 200-line function. **Complexity accumulates.** ::: ::: {.notes} `demo-next` -> 04-complexity. First run Pyright: it should pass. Then Ruff: C901 should fail. Anecdote slot: function that became frightening to modify. ::: --- ## So… is it correct? - Reproducible environment ✓ - Formatted and linted ✓ - Type checked ✓ - Complexity flagged for refactoring ✓ ::: {.fragment .big-question} **Is the answer right?** ::: ::: {.fragment} **We don't know.** None of those tools knows what a reaction time means. ::: --- ## Types aren't domain knowledge ```text participant condition reaction_time_ms P01 control -250 ``` | Question | Verdict | |---|:---:| | Valid number? | ✓ | | Valid float? | ✓ | | Ruff? | ✓ | | Pyright? | ✓ | | Scientifically plausible? | **✗** | ::: {.fragment .takeaway} A value can have the correct type and still be wrong. ::: --- ## Encode what “correct” means ```python if (reaction_times <= 0).any(): raise ValueError( "Reaction times must be greater than zero." ) ``` ::: {.fragment} ```python def test_negative_reaction_times_are_rejected(): # synthetic test data containing -250 ms ... ``` ::: ::: {.fragment} ```bash uv run pytest ``` ::: ::: {.notes} `demo-next` -> 05-tests. Use synthetic invalid data for the domain-validation example. Do not edit raw data. Explain: if real raw data fail validation, investigate provenance or use a documented processing/correction step. ::: --- ## Different tools catch different failures | Problem | Ruff | Pyright | Complexity | pytest | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Unused import | ✓ | | | | | Wrong argument type | | ✓ | | | | Branch-heavy function | | | ✓ | | | Invalid domain value | | | | ✓* | | Wrong filtering logic | | | | ✓ | * Because we encoded the domain rule. ::: {.takeaway .fragment} There isn't one “code quality” tool. They answer different questions. ::: --- ## Valid code can still be wrong Change: ```python correct = data[data["correct"]] ``` into: ```python correct = data[~data["correct"]] ``` ::: {.fragment} ```text Ruff ✓ Pyright ✓ pytest ✗ ``` ::: ::: {.takeaway .fragment} The code is valid, formatted and type-correct. **It just does the opposite of what I intended.** ::: ::: {.notes} This is the strongest live demo. At 05-tests, make the temporary inversion. Run Ruff, Pyright, then pytest. Use `demo-reset` afterwards. ::: --- ## There's still a bug in the system ```text Developer │ │ remember to run... ▼ ┌─────────┐ │ Ruff │ │ Pyright │ │ pytest │ └─────────┘ ``` ::: {.fragment .big-question} The fragile component is **remember**. ::: --- ## Automate the discipline ```text git commit │ ▼ pre-commit │ ├── Ruff ├── Pyright └── pytest ``` ::: {.fragment} ```bash git commit -m "Demonstrate pre-commit" ``` ::: ::: {.fragment .takeaway} Make the easiest workflow the correct workflow. ::: ::: {.notes} `demo-next` -> 06-precommit. Add an unused import, stage it, attempt commit; hook should stop it. Then mention `git commit --no-verify` to motivate CI. ::: --- ## Your laptop isn't the authority ```text GitHub │ ▼ fresh environment │ ┌────────┼────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Ruff Pyright pytest │ │ │ └────────┼────────┘ ▼ ✓ / ✗ ``` ::: {.takeaway .fragment} Local automation improves my workflow. **CI independently verifies the shared project.** ::: ::: {.notes} `demo-next` -> 07-ci. Use a prepared branch or screenshot/video backup. Demonstrate a --no-verify commit being rejected by GitHub Actions. ::: --- ## Software doesn't stop changing ```text time → Python ─────────────────► pandas ─────────────────► Ruff ─────────────────► Actions ─────────────────► your code ────────────────── ``` ::: {.fragment} ```text Dependency update │ ▼ automatic PR │ ▼ CI │ ▼ Do the tests still pass? ``` ::: ::: {.notes} `demo-next` -> 08-dependabot. Show a prepared Dependabot PR rather than waiting for one live. Message: automated updates become safer because tests and CI already exist. ::: --- ## Give the project a vocabulary Before: ```bash uv run ruff check . uv run ruff format --check . uv run pyright uv run pytest uv run python -m rt_analysis.figure ``` ::: {.fragment} After: ```bash make check make figure ``` ::: ::: {.takeaway .fragment} A Makefile gives the project a **vocabulary**. ::: ::: {.notes} `demo-next` -> 09-final. Run `make check`, then `make figure`. Anecdote slot: forgetting the sequence required to regenerate an analysis/output. ::: --- ## Reduce friction ```text Good practice + unnecessary friction │ ▼ eventually gets skipped ``` ::: {.fragment} **Make** — project-level shortcuts **Espanso** — personal repetitive-text shortcuts ::: ::: {.fragment .takeaway} Make desirable behaviour cheap. ::: ::: {.notes} Show one real Espanso shortcut from your workflow. Keep this brief. ::: --- ## Can you reproduce Figure 1 now? ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="38%"} ### Before ```text analysis.py data/ └── results.csv ``` ::: ::: {.column width="62%"} ### After ```text .github/ data/ src/ └── rt_analysis/ tests/ .pre-commit-config.yaml Makefile README.md pyproject.toml uv.lock ``` ::: ::: ::: {.fragment} ```bash uv sync make check make figure ``` ::: --- ## Which project is simpler? ::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="45%"} ### The first - fewer files - fewer concepts - quicker to start ::: ::: {.column width="55%"} ### The second - environment encoded - assumptions tested - checks automated - workflow documented ::: ::: ::: {.fragment .big-question} The first has fewer files. **The second has fewer unstated assumptions.** ::: --- ## The same ideas exist elsewhere | Purpose | Python | JS / TS | R | Praat | |---|---|---|---|---| | Environment/deps | uv | pnpm / npm | renv | manual | | Format/lint | Ruff | ESLint + Prettier | lintr + styler | conventions | | Types | Pyright | TypeScript | limited | — | | Complexity | Ruff C901 | ESLint | cyclocomp | manual | | Tests | pytest | Vitest / Jest | testthat | regression scripts | | Hooks | pre-commit | Husky / lint-staged | pre-commit | external | | CI | GitHub Actions | GitHub Actions | GitHub Actions | possible externally | | Updates | Dependabot | Dependabot | ecosystem-dependent | manual | | Tasks | Make | Make / npm scripts | Make | Make | ::: {.takeaway .fragment} Don't learn the brand names. **Learn the problems they solve.** ::: --- ## Where should I start? ::: {.incremental} 1. **Git + reproducible environment** 2. **Formatter / linter** 3. **Tests** 4. **Types** where useful 5. **Pre-commit** 6. **CI** as the project becomes shared/important 7. **Dependency and task automation** ::: ::: {.fragment .takeaway} Adopt tooling when you understand the problem it is solving. ::: --- ## Move failures earlier ```text while typing Ruff / Pyright │ ▼ before commit tests / complexity │ ▼ at commit pre-commit │ ▼ after push CI │ ▼ later collaborator / user │ ▼ latest published result ``` ::: {.fragment} **Catch mistakes sooner.** **Make assumptions explicit.** **Automate what you'll forget.** **Make the correct workflow easy.** ::: ::: {.notes} Closing message: professional tooling is largely about moving failures earlier and reducing hidden assumptions. :::
